definition_en: to collect or increase in quantity gradually over a period of time
core_image: 雪球顺着斜坡滚下，一路把新雪粘到身上
scene: 老屋已经很久没人住了，琴盖上落了厚厚一层灰。Dust had accumulated on the old piano.
sceneCN: 这里的 accumulate 是「堆积」（第 2 个义项：东西一点点堆在一处）；句意是旧钢琴上积了一层灰。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「积累；堆积物」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「累积的」
由词干加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「蓄能器；累加器」

senses.title: To build up something valuable
senses.definition: to gather more and more of something useful or valuable over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间推移，把有用的或有价值的东西越聚越多
senses.example: She accumulated a large collection of rare books.
senses.exampleCN: 她积累了一大批珍本书。
senses.why: The Latin noun cumulus names a heap, and ad- points things towards it, so the verb pictures valuables being heaped into one store.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 cumulus 指「堆」，前缀 ad- 表示「朝着一处」，所以这个词画出的是把有价值的东西往同一个仓里堆。

senses.title: To pile up in one place
senses.definition: to collect in a growing pile, usually without anyone arranging it
senses.definitionCN: 东西无人整理地越堆越多，聚在一处
senses.example: Snow accumulated against the garden wall.
senses.exampleCN: 雪在院墙边越积越高。
senses.why: The same heap image turns literal: snow, dust and papers have no owner adding them, yet they still form a cumulus.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「堆」的意象在这里变成实景：雪、灰和纸张并没有人刻意去添，却照样堆成一个土丘似的形状。

senses.title: To grow in intensity
senses.definition: to increase gradually until a feeling or problem becomes strong
senses.definitionCN: 情绪或问题逐渐加重，直到变得强烈
senses.example: Tension accumulated between the two neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 两个邻居之间的紧张情绪越积越重。
senses.why: A heap can be made of feelings as well as objects; each small grievance adds one more layer until the mass presses down.
senses.whyCN: 堆起来的不只是实物，也可以是情绪；每一次小小的不满都加一层，最后整堆重量压了下来。

intro.en: The word is Latin in both parts: a prefix of direction and a noun for a heap.
intro.cn: 这个词的两半都来自拉丁语：一个表示方向的前缀，一个表示「堆」的名词。

items.en: cumulus meant a heap, a mass or a pile.
items.cn: cumulus 意为堆、团、垛。

items.en: accumulare joined ad-, towards, with cumulus, to heap something up.
items.cn: accumulare 把表示「朝向」的 ad- 与 cumulus 结合，意为把东西堆起来。

items.en: the participle accumulatus described what had been piled together.
items.cn: 分词 accumulatus 描述已经堆在一起的东西。

items.en: accumulate entered English as a learned verb of heaping and adding.
items.cn: accumulate 在十五世纪进入英语，是书面语中表示「堆叠、添加」的动词。

items.en: it now covers money, data, experience, dust and even stress.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖金钱、数据、经验、灰尘，甚至压力。

note.en: The first group is the cumulus family; the second is other verbs of collecting.
note.cn: 第一组是 cumulus 词族；第二组是别的表示收集的动词。

entries.definition: the process or result of heaping things up
tending to grow by repeated addition
a device that stores energy or numbers
to collect a large amount of something
to bring things together in one place
to form a heap through repeated addition
to bring items together as a set

normalIntro.en: These hints follow cumulus, the Latin heap at the centre of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条都围绕词心的拉丁语 cumulus（堆）。

normal.en: cumulus is Latin for a heap, and it also gives us the cloud name.
normal.cn: cumulus 是拉丁语的「堆」，积云的名字也来自它。

normal.en: ad- means towards, so the verb is literally to heap towards one point.
normal.cn: ad- 意为「朝向」，所以这个词字面上就是往一点上堆。

normal.en: -ate marks the Latin verb, parallel to calculate and estimate.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 标记拉丁动词，与 calculate、estimate 同一套路。

normal.en: accumulation is the noun, and accumulative describes the growing kind.
normal.cn: accumulation 是名词，accumulative 形容「越积越多」的那一类。

normal.en: the verb keeps company with wealth, knowledge, evidence and dust.
normal.cn: 这个词常与财富、知识、证据、灰尘这些宾语同现。

abstract.en: Watch a snowball roll downhill and swell with every turn.
abstract.cn: 想象雪球滚下坡，每转一圈就胖一圈。

abstract.en: Picture coins dropping into a glass jar until it is full.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币一枚枚落进玻璃罐，直到装满。

abstract.en: See layers of dust settle on a forgotten piano.
abstract.cn: 想象灰尘一层层落在一架被遗忘的钢琴上。

examples.en: Small savings accumulate quickly if you add to them each month.
examples.cn: 如果每月都添一点，小笔储蓄很快就会累积起来。

examples.en: Letters accumulated on the desk while she was away.
examples.cn: 她外出期间，桌上的信越堆越多。

examples.en: He accumulated enough evidence to prove his case.
examples.cn: 他收集到了足以证明自己主张的证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿丘缪累特」——阿丘把东西一件件往怀里搂，越搂越沉，累得直喘。

root: 拉丁语 accumulare（堆起来），由 ad-（朝向）与 cumulus（堆）构成；本义是把东西往一处堆，后引申为数量逐渐增多。

sensesIntro.en: One heap image serves three scales: valuables stored up, objects piling on their own, and feelings pressing down.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「堆」的意象管着三种尺度：存起来的值钱物、自己堆高的实物、以及压下来的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap that grows layer by layer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层一层长高的堆。

branches.en: money, books and knowledge stored up on purpose
branches.cn: 有意存起来的钱、书与知识

branches.en: snow, dust and paper gathering without a keeper
branches.cn: 无人照看而自行堆积的雪、灰与纸张

branches.en: grievances and tension adding weight
branches.cn: 不断加重的不满与紧张

branches.en: invisible things that still behave like a heap
branches.cn: 虽无形却仍像堆一样增长的东西

branches.en: quantity rising whether or not someone intends it
branches.cn: 不管有意无意，数量都在往上走

intro.en: A Latin prefix, a Latin noun and a verb ending make the whole word.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁名词和一个动词词尾，拼成了整个词。

latinIntro.en: The heap root cumulus also appears in cumulative and in the cloud name cumulus.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「堆」的词根 cumulus 也出现在 cumulative 和云名 cumulus 里。

definition_en: the process of gradually collecting something, or the amount collected
core_image: 仓库角落里的箱子一年年往上码
scene: 机翼上的冰越结越厚，飞行员开始担心。The accumulation of ice on the wings worried the pilot.
sceneCN: 这里的 accumulation 是「堆积过程」（第 1 个义项：逐渐积聚起来）；句意是机翼结冰让飞行员担心。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「积累；堆积」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「累积的」
由词干加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「蓄能器」

senses.title: The process of building up
senses.definition: the gradual process by which something increases in amount
senses.definitionCN: 某物数量逐渐增多的过程
senses.example: The accumulation of data took several years.
senses.exampleCN: 数据的积累花了几年时间。
senses.why: The noun ending turns the act of heaping into a process, so the word names the slow adding rather than the heap itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词词尾把「堆」这个动作变作过程，所以这个词指的是慢慢添加的过程，而不是堆本身。

senses.title: A mass that has piled up
senses.definition: an amount of something that has gathered into a mass
senses.definitionCN: 已经聚成一团或一层的一定量东西
senses.example: An accumulation of leaves blocked the drain.
senses.exampleCN: 积起来的落叶堵住了排水口。
senses.why: Once the process stops, what is left is a visible mass; English uses the same noun for the result and the activity.
senses.whyCN: 过程一停，留下的就是看得见的一团；英语用同一个名词兼指动作与结果。

intro.en: The noun is the Latin action noun built on the verb for heaping.
intro.cn: 这个名词是拉丁语中由「堆」的动词构成的动作名词。

items.en: cumulus named a heap or a rounded mass.
items.cn: cumulus 指堆或圆团。

items.en: accumulare meant to heap something up.
items.cn: accumulare 意为把东西堆起来。

items.en: accumulatio named the act of heaping.
items.cn: accumulatio 指「堆叠」这一行为。

items.en: accumulation entered English as a scholarly noun of increase.
items.cn: accumulation 在十六世纪进入英语，是书面语中表示「增多」的名词。

items.en: it now appears in finance, science and everyday talk of clutter.
items.cn: 如今它出现在金融、科学以及日常谈杂物堆积的场合。

note.en: The first group shares the heap root; the second names other kinds of increase.
note.cn: 第一组共享「堆」的词根；第二组是别的表示增多的说法。

entries.definition: to heap something up over time
something that stores what is added
a group of things brought together
a heap of objects resting on one another
a supply stored up for future use

normalIntro.en: Everything here hangs on the Latin heap cumulus.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条都挂在拉丁语的「堆」cumulus 上。

normal.en: cumulus is the heap, and -ation turns heaping into a process.
normal.cn: cumulus 是「堆」，-ation 把「堆」变成过程。

normal.en: the same noun serves both the act and the pile left behind.
normal.cn: 同一个名词既指动作，也指留下来的那堆东西。

normal.en: capital accumulation is a fixed phrase in economics.
normal.cn: capital accumulation 是经济学里的固定说法。

normal.en: dust accumulation is the everyday version of the same idea.
normal.cn: dust accumulation 是同一想法在日常里的版本。

normal.en: the plural accumulations usually points to several separate piles.
normal.cn: 复数 accumulations 通常指分开的几堆。

abstract.en: See boxes stacked higher in a warehouse corner each year.
abstract.cn: 想象仓库角落的箱子一年比一年码得高。

abstract.en: Picture a layer of ice thickening on a wing.
abstract.cn: 想象机翼上的冰层一点点变厚。

abstract.en: Think of a bank statement where interest keeps adding to the balance.
abstract.cn: 想象银行账单上利息不断并进余额。

examples.en: The accumulation of evidence finally convinced the judge.
examples.cn: 证据的不断累积最终说服了法官。

examples.en: An accumulation of sand had blocked the road.
examples.cn: 堆积的沙子堵住了道路。

examples.en: Slow accumulation of skills made him a fine craftsman.
examples.cn: 技艺的慢慢积累使他成了好工匠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿丘缪累身」——阿丘把东西越堆越多，最后累到自己身上。

root: 拉丁语 accumulatio，源自 accumulare（堆起来），词根 cumulus 意为「堆」；本义是堆叠的动作，后指积累的过程与积成之物。

sensesIntro.en: The noun looks at the heap from two sides: the slow adding, and the mass that remains.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从两面看同一堆东西：慢慢添加的过程，以及最后留下的那团。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pile still growing, then standing finished.
core.cn: 核心意象：一边还在长高、一边已经成形的堆。

branches.en: the slow adding of data, capital or skill
branches.cn: 数据、资本或技艺的缓慢添加

branches.en: the visible heap of leaves, sand or ice
branches.cn: 看得见的落叶、沙子或冰层

branches.en: an action that leaves a tangible result
branches.cn: 留下实物的那个动作

branches.en: time as the quiet agent of increase
branches.cn: 时间作为无声的增长者

branches.en: quantity you can measure and clear away
branches.cn: 可以丈量、也可以清走的数量

intro.en: A Latin verb stem plus a noun ending carries the whole idea of heaping.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁动词词干加一个名词词尾，就承载了「堆」的全部意思。

latinIntro.en: cumulus, the heap, is also the root of cumulative and of the cloud name.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「堆」的 cumulus 也是 cumulative 和云名 cumulus 的词根。

definition_en: the quality of being correct or exact
core_image: 一支箭正落在靶心的十字交点上
scene: 天气预报说准了下雨的时间，农民都很惊讶。The accuracy of the forecast surprised the farmers.
sceneCN: 这里的 accuracy 是「与事实相符的准确」（第 1 个义项：信息正确）；句意是预报之准让农民吃惊。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀构成形容词，义为「准确的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「准确地」
加否定前缀构成，义为「不准确；误差」
加否定前缀构成，义为「不准确的」

senses.title: Fidelity to the facts
senses.definition: the quality of being correct and true in matters of fact
senses.definitionCN: 在事实层面正确、无误的性质
senses.example: Nobody doubted the accuracy of her report.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人怀疑她报告的准确性。
senses.why: The Latin root cura means care, so accuracy first names the care that keeps a statement from drifting away from the truth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 cura 意为「用心」，所以 accuracy 最初指的是那份让陈述不偏离事实的用心。

senses.title: Closeness of a measurement
senses.definition: the degree to which a measurement or calculation matches the true value
senses.definitionCN: 测量或计算结果与真实值接近的程度
senses.example: The accuracy of the scale was tested with known weights.
senses.exampleCN: 人们用已知重量的砝码检测这台秤的精度。
senses.why: An instrument shows its care by repeating the same true value; the noun moves from honest speech to calibrated metal.
senses.whyCN: 仪器靠反复给出同一个真实值来体现「用心」，这个词于是从说实话挪到了校准过的金属上。

senses.title: Steadiness in hitting a target
senses.definition: the ability to send a shot or throw to the intended point
senses.definitionCN: 把射击或投掷送到预定点的能力
senses.example: Her accuracy with a bow improved after months of practice.
senses.exampleCN: 练了几个月后，她的射箭准头提高了。
senses.why: Here the true value is a point on a target, and care becomes the steady hand that repeats the same aim.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「真实值」是靶上的一个点，而「用心」变成了那只每次都瞄准同一点、稳稳不放的手。

intro.en: The word grows from Latin care, not from a root meaning sharp or fast.
intro.cn: 这个词长自拉丁语的「用心」，而不是表示锋利或快速的字根。

items.en: cura meant care, attention or trouble taken over something.
items.cn: cura 意为关心、留意，或为某事费的心。

items.en: accuratus described something done with care and therefore exact.
items.cn: accuratus 形容某事做得用心，因而精确。

items.en: the noun accuratio named careful exactness.
items.cn: 名词 accuratio 指用心的精确。

items.en: accuracy entered English as a noun of exactness in statement and measure.
items.cn: accuracy 在十七世纪进入英语，指陈述与度量上的精确。

items.en: it now covers news reports, laboratory data and rifle scores.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖新闻报道、实验室数据与射击成绩。

note.en: The first group is the accurate family; the second is other words for exactness.
note.cn: 第一组是 accurate 词族；第二组是别的表示精确的说法。

entries.definition: in a correct and exact way
the quality of being exact and repeatable
closeness to an original or a fact

normalIntro.en: The key is Latin cura, care, which also lives in cure and curator.
normalIntro.cn: 关键是拉丁语 cura（用心），cure、curator 里也有它。

normal.en: cura means care, so accuracy is the fruit of taking care.
normal.cn: cura 意为用心，accuracy 就是用心的果实。

normal.en: the adjective accurate drops the noun ending and keeps the stem.
normal.cn: 形容词 accurate 去掉名词词尾，保留同一个词干。

normal.en: in- before accuracy reverses it into error.
normal.cn: 在 accuracy 前加 in- 就翻成误差。

normal.en: measurement accuracy and accuracy rate are the usual technical pairs.
normal.cn: measurement accuracy 与 accuracy rate 是常见的技术搭配。

normal.en: pinpoint accuracy is the phrase for an almost perfect hit.
normal.cn: pinpoint accuracy 形容几乎分毫不差的命中。

abstract.en: See an arrow settle exactly in the centre of the target.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭不偏不倚扎进靶心。

abstract.en: Picture a scale needle stopping on the true weight.
abstract.cn: 想象秤的指针停在真实重量上。

abstract.en: Think of a reporter checking every name twice before printing.
abstract.cn: 想象记者发稿前把每个人名核了两遍。

examples.en: The accuracy of the map saved the hikers from a wrong turn.
examples.cn: 地图的准确让徒步者免于走错路。

examples.en: Modern instruments measure temperature with great accuracy.
examples.cn: 现代仪器能非常精确地测量温度。

examples.en: His accuracy at the dartboard impressed the whole pub.
examples.cn: 他在飞镖盘前的准头让整个酒馆都佩服。

root: 拉丁语 accuratus（用心的、精确的），源自 ad-（朝向）与 cura（关心、留意）；本义是「用心做」，引申为与事实或真值相符。

sensesIntro.en: One idea of care branches into honest words, calibrated instruments and steady aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「用心」分作三支：诚实的话、校准的仪器、稳定的瞄准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark that lands exactly where it should.
core.cn: 核心意象：落在应落之处的那个点。

branches.en: a report that matches what really happened
branches.cn: 与实际发生之事相符的报道

branches.en: an instrument that returns the true value
branches.cn: 给出真实值的仪器

branches.en: a hand that sends the shot to the mark
branches.cn: 把箭送到靶点的那只手

branches.en: care shown both in speech and in action
branches.cn: 说话与动作里同样体现的用心

branches.en: numbers you can trust because someone checked them
branches.cn: 因为有人核对过而可信的数字

intro.en: A Latin care-root, a participle ending and a noun suffix build the word.
intro.cn: 一个表示「用心」的拉丁词根、一个分词词尾和一个名词后缀，构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: cura, care, also gives cure, curator and curious through related Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: cura（用心）经由相关拉丁形式也给出 cure、curator 与 curious。

definition_en: correct in every detail and free from error
core_image: 尺子边缘与木料边沿严丝合缝
scene: 这张地图连最窄的小巷都标对了。The map is accurate down to the smallest street.
sceneCN: 这里的 accurate 是「与事实相符的」（第 1 个义项：细节正确）；句意是地图连小巷都标得准。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「准确性」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「准确地」
加否定前缀构成，义为「不准确的」
由不准确形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「误差」

senses.title: Correct in the details
senses.definition: giving all the details correctly and saying nothing false
senses.definitionCN: 细节全都正确，没有说错的地方
senses.example: The witness gave an accurate account of the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 目击者对撞车经过作了准确描述。
senses.why: The Latin past participle says done with care; a careful account is one whose details all match the event.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语分词的意思是「用心做成的」；用心的陈述，就是每个细节都与事件对得上。

senses.title: Precise as a measurement
senses.definition: measured or calculated to a value very close to the truth
senses.definitionCN: 测量或计算出的数值非常接近真实值
senses.example: The thermometer gives an accurate reading within seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这支温度计几秒内就给出精确读数。
senses.why: When care is applied to instruments, the adjective describes a number that stops at the true value instead of near it.
senses.whyCN: 当「用心」落到仪器上，这个形容词就形容一个停在真值上、而不是差一点点的数字。

senses.title: On target
senses.definition: sent to the intended point, as of a shot or throw
senses.definitionCN: 射击或投掷被送到预定点上的
senses.example: One accurate throw knocked the can off the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 一次精准的投掷把罐子从墙上打落。
senses.why: A target is a physical fact to be matched, so the same care becomes a steady hand and a true line.
senses.whyCN: 靶子是必须对上的物理事实，于是同一份「用心」变成了稳定的手和笔直的轨迹。

intro.en: The adjective is the Latin participle of a verb meaning to do with care.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是拉丁语中表示「用心去做」的动词的分词。

items.en: cura meant care and attention.
items.cn: cura 意为关心与留意。

items.en: accurare meant to take care over something.
items.cn: accurare 意为对某事用心。

items.en: accuratus, the past participle, described what had been done carefully.
items.cn: 过去分词 accuratus 形容已经用心做成的东西。

items.en: accurate entered English as an adjective of careful exactness.
items.cn: accurate 在十六世纪进入英语，形容用心的精确。

items.en: it now modifies reports, scales, clocks and throws.
items.cn: 如今它修饰报道、天平、钟表和投掷。

normalIntro.en: The word carries Latin cura, care, at its core.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的核心是拉丁语 cura，也就是「用心」。

normal.en: cura is care, and accurate means made with care.
normal.cn: cura 是用心，accurate 就是用心的结果。

normal.en: the ending -ate marks a Latin participle turned adjective.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 标记由拉丁分词转来的形容词。

normal.en: put in- in front and the care disappears: inaccurate.
normal.cn: 前面加 in-，那份用心就消失了：inaccurate。

normal.en: accurate to three decimal places is a common technical phrase.
normal.cn: accurate to three decimal places 是常见的技术说法。

normal.en: highly accurate is the usual way to praise a forecast or a device.
normal.cn: 夸预报或仪器时常用 highly accurate。

abstract.en: See a ruler edge sitting flush against a cut board.
abstract.cn: 想象尺子边缘紧贴切好的木板，严丝合缝。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands land on the exact minute.
abstract.cn: 想象钟的指针正好落在整分上。

abstract.en: Think of a witness naming every detail without a pause.
abstract.cn: 想象目击者毫不迟疑地说出每个细节。

examples.en: Her description of the room was accurate in every detail.
examples.cn: 她对那个房间的描述每个细节都准确。

examples.en: The test gives an accurate picture of your fitness.
examples.cn: 这项测试能准确反映你的体能状况。

examples.en: An accurate shot from the edge won the match.
examples.cn: 边线上一记精准的射门赢下了比赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克尤瑞特」——阿克量木料时把尺子贴得特紧，一毫米都不肯差。

root: 拉丁语 accuratus（用心的、精细的），源自 ad-（朝向）与 cura（关心）；本义是「用心做成」，引申为细节正确、数值精确。

sensesIntro.en: The same care shows up as true words, true numbers and a true aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一份用心，表现为真话、真数与真正的准头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an edge that meets the line without a gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：边沿与线严丝合缝、不留缝。

branches.en: a story whose details all check out
branches.cn: 每个细节都经得起核对的叙述

branches.en: a reading that stops at the true value

branches.en: a throw that reaches the intended point
branches.cn: 到达预定点的投掷

branches.en: exactness shared by words and numbers
branches.cn: 言语与数字共有的精确

branches.en: a value and a target both hit dead on
branches.cn: 数值与靶心都被正中

intro.en: A Latin care-root plus a participle ending yields the adjective.
intro.cn: 一个表示「用心」的拉丁词根加上分词词尾，就得到这个形容词。

latinIntro.en: cura, care, also underlies cure and curator.
latinIntro.cn: cura（用心）也是 cure 与 curator 的底层词根。

definition_en: in a way that is correct and free from error
core_image: 报站员一字不差地念出站名和时间
scene: 护士把药量抽到刻度线上，又核对了一遍。The nurse measured the dose accurately.
sceneCN: 这里的 accurately 是「精确地」（第 2 个义项：测量数值准确）；句意是护士把药量量得很准。

derivatives.zh: 由副词去后缀还原为形容词，义为「准确的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「准确性」
加否定前缀构成，义为「不准确的」

senses.title: Without misstating the facts
senses.definition: in a way that reports the facts correctly
senses.definitionCN: 以符合事实、没有说错的方式
senses.example: She accurately described the man at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她准确描述了门口那个男人的样子。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the Latin idea of care and applies it to speech: every detail is checked before it is said.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词保留了拉丁语「用心」的意思，并把它用在说话上：每个细节都先核对再说出口。

senses.title: With a precise reading
senses.definition: with numbers or amounts that come very close to the true value
senses.definitionCN: 所用数值或分量非常接近真实值地
senses.example: The device accurately records the room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这台设备能精确记录室内温度。
senses.why: Care moves from words to instruments, and the adverb now describes how a needle or a meter lands on the true figure.
senses.whyCN: 「用心」从言语挪到仪器上，这个副词便形容指针或仪表如何落在真实数值上。

senses.title: With a true aim
senses.definition: in a way that sends something to the intended point
senses.definitionCN: 把东西送到预定点上地
senses.example: He threw the ball accurately into the basket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把球精准地投进了篮筐。
senses.why: A target gives care a visible test, so the adverb marks the throw whose line ends exactly where the eye intended.
senses.whyCN: 靶子给「用心」一个看得见的检验，于是这个副词标记出那条终点正合心意的投掷线。

intro.en: The adverb is the Latin care adjective plus the English manner ending.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语的「用心」形容词加英语方式词尾构成。

items.en: cura meant care and attention.
items.cn: cura 意为关心与留意。

items.en: accuratus described work done with care.
items.cn: accuratus 形容用心做成的活。

items.en: accurate came into English as an adjective of exactness.
items.cn: accurate 作为表示精确的形容词进入英语。

items.en: the ending -ly turned it into an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把它变成方式副词。

items.en: accurately now modifies verbs of describing, measuring and aiming.
items.cn: 如今 accurately 修饰描述、测量与瞄准一类动词。

note.en: The first group is the accurate family; the second is other adverbs of exactness.
note.cn: 第一组是 accurate 词族；第二组是别的表示精确的副词。

entries.definition: in an exact and careful way
in a way that is right
in a way that stays true to the original

normalIntro.en: The adverb is simply accurate plus the manner ending -ly.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词就是 accurate 加方式词尾 -ly。

normal.en: accurate plus -ly gives the manner of doing something with care.
normal.cn: accurate 加 -ly，得到「用心去做」的方式。

normal.en: the base cura means care, so the adverb never means fast.
normal.cn: 词根 cura 意为用心，所以这个副词从不表示「快」。

normal.en: it pairs naturally with describe, measure, predict and report.
normal.cn: 它天然与 describe、measure、predict、report 搭配。

normal.en: in- on the adjective turns it into its opposite.
normal.cn: 形容词前加 in- 就得到反义。

normal.en: more and most form the comparative and superlative.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级分别用 more 和 most。

abstract.en: Hear a station announcer reading every name without a slip.
abstract.cn: 想象报站员把每个站名都念得一字不差。

abstract.en: See a nurse lining the syringe up with the mark.
abstract.cn: 想象护士把针筒对准刻度线。

abstract.en: Picture a ball dropping cleanly through the hoop.
abstract.cn: 想象球干干净净地穿过篮筐。

examples.en: The guide accurately described the route up the mountain.
examples.cn: 向导准确描述了上山路线。

examples.en: This watch keeps time accurately even in cold weather.
examples.cn: 这块表在寒冷天气里也走得很准。

examples.en: She accurately predicted the result of the vote.
examples.cn: 她准确预测了投票结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克尤瑞特利」——阿克每做一步都回头核对，做事特利落又特准。

root: 由 accurate（拉丁语 accuratus，用心的、精确的）加副词词尾 -ly 构成；核心仍是 cura（关心、留意），表示以用心、无误的方式去做。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb carries one kind of care into three arenas: speech, measurement and aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词把同一种「用心」带进三个场域：说话、测量与瞄准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that checks before it moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：动手之前先核对的那只手。

branches.en: words that match the scene described
branches.cn: 与所述场景相符的言语

branches.en: instruments that stop at the true figure
branches.cn: 停在真实数值上的仪器

branches.en: a throw that ends on the chosen point
branches.cn: 落在选定点上的投掷

branches.en: exactness in both words and numbers
branches.cn: 言语与数字两方面的精确

branches.en: a reading and a shot that both hit true
branches.cn: 读数与投射都正中目标

intro.en: A Latin care stem, an adjective ending and an adverb ending make the word.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「用心」词干、形容词词尾与副词词尾，三者拼成这个词。

latinIntro.en: The care root cura is also behind cure and curator.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「用心」的词根 cura 也藏在 cure 与 curator 后面。

definition_en: a statement saying that someone has done something wrong
core_image: 一根手指直直指向对面的人
scene: 他声音平静，否认了那项指控。He denied the accusation with a calm voice.
sceneCN: 这里的 accusation 是「指控」（第 1 个义项：正式说某人有错）；句意是他平静地否认了指控。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「指控；指责」
由动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「被指控的」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「指控者」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「指责的」

senses.title: A formal charge against someone
senses.definition: a public statement that a person has committed a crime or a serious fault
senses.definitionCN: 公开指出某人犯了罪或有严重过失的话
senses.example: The accusation was read aloud in court.
senses.exampleCN: 那项指控在法庭上被大声宣读。
senses.why: The Latin causa means a lawsuit, so the noun began as the act of bringing a case rather than a private complaint.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 causa 意为「诉讼」，所以这个名词最初指把案子提上法庭的行为，而不是私下的抱怨。

senses.title: The charge itself
senses.definition: the particular wrong that someone is said to have done
senses.definitionCN: 某人被说成做过的那件具体的错事
senses.example: The accusation against him was theft.
senses.exampleCN: 对他的指控是盗窃。
senses.why: Once a case is opened, the word shifts from the act of charging to the content of the charge, the thing written in the file.
senses.whyCN: 案子一立，词义就从「提出指控」转到「指控的内容」，也就是写进卷宗的那一条。

senses.title: An informal charge of blame
senses.definition: a claim of blame made outside any court
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭之外提出的责备性说法
senses.example: Her accusation hurt him more than the fine.
senses.exampleCN: 她的指责比罚款更伤他。
senses.why: A lawsuit can shrink to a quarrel; the same pointing finger now appears at the dinner table rather than the dock.
senses.whyCN: 诉讼可以缩成一场争吵；同一根指点的手指，如今出现在餐桌边，而不是被告席前。

intro.en: The noun comes from the Latin verb for bringing a case, built on the word for a lawsuit.
intro.cn: 这个名词来自拉丁语中「提起诉讼」的动词，其词根是「诉讼」。

items.en: causa meant a cause, a case or a lawsuit.
items.cn: causa 意为原因、案件或诉讼。

items.en: accusare meant to call someone to account before a court.
items.cn: accusare 意为在法庭上追究某人。

items.en: accusatio named the act of bringing such a charge.
items.cn: accusatio 指提出这种指控的行为。

items.en: the form passed through Old French before reaching English.
items.cn: 这个词形先经过古法语，再进入英语。

items.en: the noun now covers courts, news stories and family quarrels.
items.cn: 如今这个名词覆盖法庭、新闻与家庭争吵。

note.en: The first group is the accuse family; the second is other words for a charge.
note.cn: 第一组是 accuse 词族；第二组是别的表示指控的说法。

normalIntro.cn: 词根 causa（诉讼）与 cause 里的那个词根是同一个。

normal.en: causa is a case or lawsuit, so accusation is born in court.
normal.cn: causa 是案件、诉讼，所以 accusation 出生在法庭。

normal.en: accuse is the verb underneath, and -ation names the act.
normal.cn: 底下的动词是 accuse，-ation 把它变成行为的名词。

normal.en: false accusation is the fixed phrase for a charge that is not true.
normal.cn: false accusation 是「不实指控」的固定说法。

normal.en: you deny or face an accusation, you do not usually answer one.
normal.cn: 常说的是 deny 或 face an accusation，一般不说 answer。

normal.en: the plural accusations often points to several separate claims.
normal.cn: 复数 accusations 常指分开的多项指控。

abstract.en: See a finger pointing straight across a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在法庭上直直指向对面。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper with one charge written on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸，上面只写了一项罪名。

abstract.en: Think of a sharp word at a dinner table that ends the meal.
abstract.cn: 想象餐桌上的一句重话，让整顿饭就此结束。

examples.en: The company denied every accusation in the report.
examples.cn: 公司否认了报告中的每一项指控。

examples.en: A false accusation can ruin a good name.
examples.cn: 不实的指控能毁掉一个好名声。

examples.en: She met the accusation with silence rather than anger.
examples.cn: 面对指责，她用沉默而不是愤怒回应。

sensesIntro.cn: 同一根指点的手指出现在三处：法庭、卷宗与餐桌。

core_image: 一个人被叫到众人面前，名字被当面点出
scene: 调查人员查出守卫收了钱，当众点了他的名。They accused the guard of taking bribes.

senses.title: To charge someone with an offence

senses.example: The police accused him of fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 警方控告他诈骗。

senses.title: To blame someone in ordinary talk

senses.definitionCN: 在没有法律程序的情况下说某人有过错
senses.example: My brother accused me of eating his cake.
senses.exampleCN: 我弟弟指责我吃了他的蛋糕。
senses.why: The courtroom finger survives in the kitchen: the same verb now points at a small fault instead of a crime.
senses.whyCN: 法庭上那根手指留到了厨房里：同一个动词现在指的是小过失，而不是罪行。

core_image: 每天走同一条石子路，脚底慢慢不再觉得硌
scene: 刚到城里时，她逼自己适应夜里的车声。She accustomed herself to the noise of the city.
sceneCN: 这里的 accustom 是「使自己习惯」（第 1 个义项：主动去适应）；句意是她让自己习惯了城里的噪声。

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转化而来，义为「习惯的；惯常的」
加否定前缀构成，义为「不习惯的」

senses.title: To make used to something
senses.definition: to train a person or an animal to accept a new condition
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复接触，让人或动物接受新的状况
senses.example: The coach accustomed the team to early training.
senses.exampleCN: 教练让队伍习惯了清早训练。
senses.why: The Old French base costume means habitual practice, so the verb is literally to turn something into a habit.
senses.whyCN: 古法语词基 costume 意为「惯常的做法」，所以这个词字面上就是「把某事变成习惯」。

senses.title: To be in the habit of
senses.definition: to have become familiar with something, usually in the phrase be accustomed to
senses.definitionCN: 已经对某事熟悉，常用于 be accustomed to 这一说法
senses.example: They are accustomed to long walks in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 他们习惯了在雨里长途步行。
senses.why: Once the training is complete, the verb's participle freezes into a state adjective: not the act of training but the settled habit.
senses.whyCN: 训练一旦完成，动词的分词就凝固成状态形容词：说的不再是训练的动作，而是安顿下来的习惯。

intro.en: The word comes through Old French, from a Latin noun for habitual practice.
intro.cn: 这个词经由古法语而来，源头是拉丁语中表示「惯常做法」的名词。

items.en: consuetudo meant custom, habit or familiar practice.
items.cn: consuetudo 意为习俗、习惯或惯常做法。

items.en: costume meant a usual manner or practice.
items.cn: 古法语 costume 意为惯常的方式或做法。

items.en: acostumer meant to make something habitual.
items.cn: acostumer 意为使某事成为习惯。

items.en: accustom entered English as a verb of training and use.
items.cn: accustom 在十五世纪进入英语，是表示训练与习惯的动词。

items.en: the participle accustomed now works as an adjective of habit.
items.cn: 分词 accustomed 如今作表示习惯的形容词使用。

note.en: The first group is the custom family; the second is other verbs of getting used.
note.cn: 第一组是 custom 词族；第二组是别的表示「使习惯」的动词。

entries.definition: to make used to something by repetition
to change in order to fit a new situation
to make someone know something well

normalIntro.en: The base custom, a habitual practice, explains the whole verb.
normalIntro.cn: 词基 custom（惯常做法）解释了整个动词。

normal.en: custom is a habit, and accustom is to turn something into one.
normal.cn: custom 是习惯，accustom 就是使某事成为习惯。

normal.en: the pattern is accustom someone to something.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 accustom someone to something。

normal.en: be accustomed to is the settled state after the training.
normal.cn: be accustomed to 是训练之后的稳定状态。

normal.en: unaccustomed puts the negative prefix on the participle.
normal.cn: unaccustomed 是在分词前加否定前缀。

normal.en: the noun custom also means the traditional practice of a group.
normal.cn: 名词 custom 也指一个群体的传统做法。

abstract.en: Walk the same stony path until your feet stop noticing.
abstract.cn: 想象每天走同一条石子路，直到脚底不再觉得硌。

abstract.en: See a new pair of shoes slowly take the shape of your foot.
abstract.cn: 想象新鞋慢慢被脚撑出形状。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer working in cold wind without complaint.
abstract.cn: 想象农人在冷风里干活，一声不吭。

examples.en: It takes time to accustom a child to a new school.
examples.cn: 让孩子习惯新学校需要时间。

examples.en: He accustomed his eyes to the dim light of the cellar.
examples.cn: 他让眼睛适应地窖里的微光。

examples.en: The villagers are accustomed to the sound of the river.
examples.cn: 村民们习惯了河水的声音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡斯特姆」——阿卡每天走同一条路，走成了一块顺脚的垫子。

root: 古法语 acostumer（使成为习惯），源自 costume（惯常做法），再上溯拉丁语 consuetudo（习俗、习惯）；本义是通过反复接触养成习惯。

sensesIntro.en: The verb has an active side, training someone, and a settled side, being used to something.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词一面是主动训练，一面是训练完成后的习惯状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: repetition wearing a path smooth.
core.cn: 核心意象：反复走动把一条路磨平。

branches.en: the active work of training someone
branches.cn: 主动训练某人的工作

branches.en: the quiet result, being used to something
branches.cn: 安静的结果：已经习惯

branches.en: coaches and teachers as the ones who accustom
branches.cn: 由教练与老师来使人习惯

branches.en: villagers who no longer hear the river
branches.cn: 已经听不见河水声的村民

branches.en: training that ends in an unremarkable habit
branches.cn: 以不起眼的习惯收尾的训练

intro.en: A French prefix, the custom stem and a verb ending build the word.
intro.cn: 一个法语前缀、custom 词干和一个动词词尾构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source consuetudo also gives consuetude, a rare formal word for custom.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头 consuetudo 也给出 consuetude 这个少见的正式词，义为习俗。

definition_en: a continuous dull pain, or to feel such a pain
core_image: 一条酸胀的腿，疼得不尖，却一直不肯停
scene: 开了整天车，他的后背一直隐隐作痛。His back ached after the long drive.
sceneCN: 这里的 ache 是「隐隐作痛」（第 2 个义项：持续性的身体疼痛）；句意是长途开车后他背疼。

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转化而来，义为「疼痛的；令人心酸的」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「酸痛的」
由 head 与 ache 复合而成，义为「头痛」

senses.title: A dull continuous pain
senses.definition: a pain that is not sharp but continues for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 不尖锐、却持续很久的疼痛
senses.example: She felt a dull ache in her knee.
senses.exampleCN: 她膝盖里有一阵钝钝的痛。
senses.why: Old English acan named a lasting bodily hurt rather than a sudden stab, so the noun keeps that slow, heavy quality.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 acan 指的是持续的身体疼痛，而不是突然的一刺，所以这个名词保留了那种缓慢、沉闷的性质。

senses.title: To hurt without stopping
senses.definition: to feel a steady dull pain in part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 身体某处持续地闷痛
senses.example: My legs ached after the long climb.
senses.exampleCN: 长途爬坡后我的腿一直酸痛。
senses.why: The same Old English verb simply turns the noun into an action: the body is doing the hurting, not holding a thing called pain.
senses.whyCN: 同一个古英语动词把名词变成动作：是身体在痛，而不是手里握着一个叫「痛」的东西。

senses.title: To long for something
senses.definition: to want something so much that it feels like a pain
senses.definitionCN: 极其想要某物，想要到像疼一样
senses.example: He ached to see his family again.
senses.exampleCN: 他渴望再见到家人。
senses.why: Emotional longing borrows the body's vocabulary: the heart hurts in the same dull way as an overtired leg.
senses.whyCN: 情感上的想念借用了身体的词：心口的闷痛，和过度劳累的腿是同一种钝法。

intro.en: The word is native English, old and Germanic, though its spelling was later reshaped.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本土的古老日耳曼词，只是拼写后来被改过。

items.en: a reconstructed root meant to hurt or to be sore.
items.cn: 一个重构词根意为疼痛、酸痛。

items.en: acan was the verb to hurt, and the noun was spelt with a k.
items.cn: acan 是表示疼痛的动词，当时名词拼写里带 k。

items.en: ake served as both noun and verb in everyday speech.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，ake 同时作名词和动词使用。

items.en: writers respelt it ache, influenced by a Greek word for pain.
items.cn: 十六世纪的写作者把它改拼为 ache，受了希腊语中表示疼痛的词影响。

items.en: the verb now also expresses longing, as in ache to see someone.
items.cn: 如今这个动词也表达渴望，如 ache to see someone。

note.en: The first group shares the ache spelling; the second is other words for pain.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ache 这个拼写；第二组是别的表示疼痛的词。

entries.definition: giving or feeling a dull pain
to beat with a strong regular pain
the state of being tender and painful

normalIntro.en: The word is short, old and native, with a spelling changed by scholars.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短、老、土生土长，只是拼写被学者改过一次。

normal.en: the old verb was acan, and the k sound survives in the pronunciation.
normal.cn: 古时的动词是 acan，那个 k 的音还留在读音里。

normal.en: the ch spelling came from a Greek word for pain, not from the root.
normal.cn: 拼写里的 ch 来自希腊语的「痛」，并不来自本词词根。

normal.en: headache and toothache show how productively ache builds compounds.
normal.cn: headache 与 toothache 显示 ache 构成复合词的能力。

normal.en: ache for is the fixed pattern for longing.
normal.cn: ache for 是表示渴望的固定搭配。

normal.en: the adjective aching often describes both legs and hearts.
normal.cn: 形容词 aching 既形容腿，也形容心。

abstract.en: Feel a heavy tiredness settling deep in the calves.
abstract.cn: 想象小腿深处压着一团沉沉的酸胀。

abstract.en: Picture a tooth that throbs with every heartbeat.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗牙随着每次心跳抽痛。

abstract.en: Think of a long absence that hurts like a bruise.
abstract.cn: 想象长久的离别像淤青一样发疼。

examples.en: A dull ache spread through her shoulders.
examples.cn: 一阵钝痛在她肩头蔓延。

examples.en: His knees ache whenever the weather turns cold.
examples.cn: 每逢天气转冷，他的膝盖就疼。

examples.en: She ached for a quiet room and an hour of sleep.
examples.cn: 她渴望一间安静的屋子和一小时的睡眠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶克」——疼得直喊「诶」，可这痛又不肯克止，一直闷着。

root: 古英语 acan（疼痛），源自日耳曼语系；本义是持续的身体疼痛，后引申为心里的渴望。拼写中的 ch 是十六世纪受希腊语 akhos（痛）影响而后加的。

sensesIntro.en: The same dull hurt runs through the noun, the verb and the longing heart.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种钝钝的痛，贯穿名词、动词与渴望的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low steady hurt that will not switch off.
core.cn: 核心意象：一直关不掉的低声疼痛。

branches.en: the ache named as a thing
branches.cn: 被当作事物命名的隐痛

branches.en: the body doing the hurting
branches.cn: 身体正在发痛

branches.en: wanting someone until it hurts
branches.cn: 想一个人想到发疼

branches.en: noun and verb for the same steady sensation
branches.cn: 名词与动词指同一种持续感觉

branches.en: pain that moves from limbs to heart
branches.cn: 从四肢移到心口的痛

intro.en: This is a native Germanic word, so its parts are old English pieces rather than Latin ones.
intro.cn: 这是本土日耳曼词，所以它的构件是古英语部件，而不是拉丁部件。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; the ch spelling was borrowed from Greek akhos by Renaissance writers.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语祖先；拼写里的 ch 是文艺复兴时期的写作者从希腊语 akhos 借来的。

definition_en: to finish something difficult successfully or reach a desired result
core_image: 登山者最后一步踏上峰顶，回头看见整条来路
scene: 比赛最后一分钟，全队终于把目标变成了现实。The team achieved its goal in the final minute.
sceneCN: 这里的 achieve 是「达到」（第 2 个义项：经过努力取得结果）；句意是全队在最后一分钟达成了目标。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「成就；达成」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「可实现的」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「有成就的人」

senses.title: To complete a difficult task
senses.definition: to bring a difficult piece of work to a successful end
senses.definitionCN: 把一件困难的工作做到成功的终点
senses.example: The crew achieved the repair before nightfall.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们在夜幕降临前完成了修理。
senses.why: The Old French source meant to come to a head or an end, so the verb first pictures a task finally reaching its finish line.
senses.whyCN: 古法语源头意为「到达顶端或终点」，所以这个动词最先画出的是一件工作终于走到终点线。

senses.title: To reach a desired result
senses.definition: to reach a goal, level or result through effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力达到某个目标、水平或结果
senses.example: She achieved the highest score in the class.
senses.exampleCN: 她取得了班里最高分。
senses.why: Once the end is reached, attention moves from the work to the reward, so the verb also names gaining a grade, a rank or a record.
senses.whyCN: 一旦走到终点，注意力就从工作本身移到收获上，于是这个词也指拿到分数、名次或纪录。

intro.en: The word reached English through Old French from the Latin word for head.
intro.cn: 这个词经由古法语进入英语，源头是拉丁语中表示「头」的词。

items.en: caput meant the head, and by extension a top or an end.
items.cn: caput 意为头，引申为顶端或终点。

items.en: chief meant the head or the leading part.
items.cn: 古法语 chief 意为头或首要部分。

items.en: achever meant to bring something to a head, hence to finish it.
items.cn: achever 意为把某事带到顶端，也就是完成它。

items.en: achieve entered English with the sense of finishing a task.
items.cn: achieve 在十四世纪进入英语，义为完成一项任务。

items.en: the sense widened from finishing work to gaining success or status.
items.cn: 词义从「完成工作」扩大到「取得成功或地位」。

note.en: The first group is the achievement family; the second is other verbs of reaching a goal.
note.cn: 第一组是 achievement 词族；第二组是别的表示达成目标的动词。

entries.definition: to reach a level or goal
to arrive at a point or aim
to make a hope or plan real

normalIntro.en: The Latin head caput is the hidden centre of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「头」caput 是这个词藏起来的中心。

normal.en: caput is head, and to achieve is to reach the head of the road.
normal.cn: caput 是头，achieve 就是走到路的顶端。

normal.en: chief and chef come from the same Latin head.
normal.cn: chief 与 chef 都出自同一个表示「头」的拉丁词。

normal.en: achievement is the noun, achievable says it can be done.
normal.cn: 名词是 achievement，achievable 表示「做得到」。

normal.en: the verb commonly takes success, a goal, results or recognition.
normal.cn: 这个动词常带 success、a goal、results 或 recognition 作宾语。

normal.en: achieve nothing is the blunt phrase for wasted effort.
normal.cn: achieve nothing 是「白费力气」的直白说法。

abstract.en: See a climber place the last step on the summit.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者把最后一步踩上峰顶。

abstract.en: Picture a runner crossing the line with arms raised.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者举手冲过终点线。

abstract.en: Think of a long list with the final item ticked.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长清单，最后一项也被划掉。

examples.en: They achieved the impossible in less than a week.
examples.cn: 他们不到一周就做成了不可能的事。

examples.en: He achieved his aim by working every evening.
examples.cn: 他每天晚上用功，达到了自己的目标。

examples.en: The small firm achieved steady growth last year.
examples.cn: 这家小公司去年取得了稳定增长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿奇夫」——阿奇一直爬到山顶，终于把「完成」两个字踩在脚下。

root: 古法语 achever（完成），源自古法语 chief（头），再上溯拉丁语 caput（头）；本义是「到达顶端」，引申为完成艰巨之事、取得成果。

sensesIntro.en: One verb looks at the end of the work and at the prize waiting there.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个动词，一面看工作的终点，一面看终点上的收获。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road that ends at a summit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条以峰顶为终点的路。

branches.en: the work brought to its finish
branches.cn: 被带到终点的工作

branches.en: the prize gained at the finish
branches.cn: 在终点得到的收获

branches.en: hands and patience finishing a repair
branches.cn: 双手与耐心完成一次修理

branches.en: scores, ranks and records obtained
branches.cn: 拿到的分数、名次与纪录

branches.en: the task and its reward in one word
branches.cn: 一个词里同时装着任务与报酬

intro.en: A French prefix, the Latin head and a verb ending make the word.
intro.cn: 一个法语前缀、拉丁语的「头」和一个动词词尾，组成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: caput, head, also gives capital, captain and chief.
latinIntro.cn: caput（头）也给出 capital、captain 与 chief。

definition_en: something important that has been done successfully, or the act of achieving it
core_image: 一块刻着名字的奖牌，被挂在墙上最亮的位置
scene: 拿到那笔奖学金，是她至今最了不起的成就。Winning the scholarship was her greatest achievement.
sceneCN: 这里的 achievement 是「成就」（第 1 个义项：做成的了不起的事）；句意是获得奖学金是她最大的成就。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「完成；达到」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「可实现的」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「有成就的人」

senses.title: A notable thing done
senses.definition: an important result that someone has produced through effort
senses.definitionCN: 某人经过努力做出的重要成果
senses.example: The bridge was a great achievement for the young engineer.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是那位年轻工程师的一大成就。
senses.why: The noun ending turns the finished act into a thing you can point at, so achievement becomes a trophy rather than a process.
senses.whyCN: 名词词尾把完成的动作变成可以指着看的「东西」，于是 achievement 成了奖杯，而不是过程。

senses.title: The act of reaching a goal
senses.definition: the successful reaching of an aim or standard
senses.definitionCN: 成功达到某个目标或标准这件事
senses.example: The achievement of independence took many years.
senses.exampleCN: 实现独立花了很多年。
senses.why: English often keeps the process reading beside the result reading, so the same noun names the reaching as well as the reached.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把「过程」与「结果」两种读法并存在同一个名词里，所以它既指到达，也指到达后的东西。

senses.title: Performance at school
senses.definition: measured success in study, especially in the phrase academic achievement
senses.definitionCN: 在学习上被衡量的成绩，尤用于 academic achievement 一语
senses.example: The school tracks the achievement of every pupil.
senses.exampleCN: 学校跟踪每个学生的学习成绩。
senses.why: In education the noun narrows to what tests and reports can measure, a score rather than a life's work.
senses.whyCN: 在教育语境里，这个词收窄成考试与报告能衡量的东西，是分数，而不是一生的功业。

intro.en: The noun is the French-style action noun of achieve, centred on the Latin head.
intro.cn: 这个名词是 achieve 的法语式动作名词，核心仍是拉丁语的「头」。

items.en: caput meant head, top or end.
items.cn: caput 意为头、顶端或终点。

items.en: achever meant to bring a matter to its head, that is, to finish it.
items.cn: achever 意为把事带到顶端，也就是完成。

items.en: the noun form added -ment to name the finished result.
items.cn: 名词形式加上 -ment，用来指完成后的结果。

items.en: achievement entered English as both a deed and a heraldic emblem.
items.cn: achievement 进入英语时既指功业，也指纹章上的标识。

items.en: it now covers personal success, school results and lifetime awards.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖个人成功、学业成绩与终身奖项。

note.en: The first group is the achieve family; the second is other words for a success.
note.cn: 第一组是 achieve 词族；第二组是别的表示成功的词。

entries.definition: the reaching of a desired aim

normalIntro.en: achieve plus -ment turns the act into a lasting record.
normalIntro.cn: achieve 加 -ment，把动作变成留得住的记录。

normal.en: the Latin head caput hides in achieve and achievement alike.
normal.cn: 拉丁语的「头」caput 同时藏在 achieve 与 achievement 里。

normal.en: sense of achievement is the feeling, not the trophy.
normal.cn: sense of achievement 指那种感觉，而不是奖杯。

normal.en: academic achievement is the school-report sense.
normal.cn: academic achievement 是成绩单上的那种意思。

normal.en: lifetime achievement is the phrase for a career's whole sum.
normal.cn: lifetime achievement 指一生事业的总和。

normal.en: the plural achievements lists separate successes.
normal.cn: 复数 achievements 列举一项项分开的成功。

abstract.en: See a medal hung on the brightest wall in the house.

senses.title: A chemical that corrodes
senses.definition: a substance that reacts with metals and turns litmus red

senses.title: Sour or corrosive in quality

senses.why: A sour taste in the mouth becomes a sour tone in the voice, so the same adjective now describes a remark that burns.

definition_zh: 承认；确认收到；致谢；示意
definition_en: to accept that something is true, or to show that you have received or noticed something
core_image: 一个人举起手，表示「我看到了，也认了」
scene: 他没有辩解，立刻承认了自己的错误。He acknowledged the mistake at once.
sceneCN: 这里的 acknowledge 是「承认」（第 1 个义项：接受某事为真）；句意是他马上承认了错误。

pos.zh: 承认；确认收到；致谢；向……示意

collocations.zh: 向某人示意已注意到他

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「承认；致谢；回执」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「公认的」
加否定前缀构成，义为「未被承认的」

senses.title: To admit that something is true
senses.definition: to accept openly that a fact or a fault is real
senses.definitionCN: 公开接受某个事实或过失确实存在
senses.example: She acknowledged that the plan had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认这个计划失败了。
senses.why: The Old English base cnawan means to know, so to acknowledge is to let what you already know be known to others.
senses.whyCN: 古英语词基 cnawan 意为「知道」，所以 acknowledge 就是把自己已经知道的事也让别人知道。

senses.title: To confirm that something arrived
senses.definition: to tell someone formally that you have received a letter, parcel or message
senses.definitionCN: 正式告知对方，信、包裹或消息已经收到
senses.example: Please acknowledge receipt of this letter.
senses.exampleCN: 请确认收到此信。
senses.why: Knowing has a practical side: once the letter is in your hand, you say so, and the knowledge becomes a receipt.
senses.whyCN: 「知道」有实际的一面：信到了手里就说一声，这份知道便成了一张回执。

senses.title: To express thanks for help
senses.definition: to publicly thank a person or a group for their help
senses.definitionCN: 公开感谢某人或某群体提供的帮助
senses.example: The author acknowledged her editor in the preface.
senses.exampleCN: 作者在序言里感谢了编辑。
senses.why: To acknowledge a debt is to admit you owe it; in print the same verb becomes a formal thank-you.
senses.whyCN: 承认欠人情，就是承认这笔账存在；写进书里，同一个动词就成了一封正式的谢辞。

senses.title: To show that you have noticed someone
senses.definition: to greet a person with a nod, a smile or a few words
senses.definitionCN: 用点头、微笑或几句话向人致意
senses.example: He acknowledged me with a brief nod.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻轻点了一下头，算是跟我打了招呼。
senses.why: The smallest form of admitting a fact is admitting a person is there; a nod says I know you without stopping.
senses.whyCN: 承认事实最小的形式，就是承认某人在场；一个点头表示「我看见你了」，却不必停下脚步。

core_image: 街角遇见一张熟悉的脸，彼此点头，却叫不出全名
scene: 在车站，我碰见了一位多年不见的熟人。I met an old acquaintance at the station.
sceneCN: 这里的 acquaintance 是「熟人」（第 1 个义项：认识但不深交的人）；句意是我在车站遇到一位旧识。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「使熟悉」
由动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「熟悉的」
由名词加抽象名词后缀构成，义为「相识关系」

senses.title: A person known slightly
senses.definition: someone you have met and recognize but do not know well
senses.definitionCN: 见过面、认得出来、但并不熟悉的人
senses.example: She is an acquaintance from my old office.
senses.exampleCN: 她是我以前办公室的一位熟人。
senses.why: The noun ending names a person rather than the act, so acquaintance becomes the face you know by name but not by heart.
senses.whyCN: 名词词尾把它指成一个人，而不是动作，于是 acquaintance 成了那个你知道名字、却不深知的人。

senses.title: Knowledge of a subject
senses.definition: a working knowledge of a field or a body of facts
senses.definitionCN: 对某个领域或一批事实的实用了解
senses.example: His acquaintance with old maps helped the search.
senses.exampleCN: 他对古地图的了解帮上了搜寻的忙。
senses.why: Knowing a person and knowing a subject are the same Latin root, so the noun also means a first-hand familiarity with facts.
senses.whyCN: 认识人与认识学问共用同一个拉丁词根，所以这个名词也指对事实的第一手熟悉。

senses.title: The relationship of knowing
senses.definition: the state of having met and being known to one another
senses.definitionCN: 彼此见过面、互相知道对方的这种关系
senses.example: Their acquaintance began at a summer school.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的相识始于一次暑期学校。
senses.why: Between the person and the knowledge lies the relation itself, and English lets the same noun name that thin thread.
senses.whyCN: 在人与其所知之间还横着关系本身，英语就让同一个名词也指这根细细的线。

intro.en: The noun is the French form of a Latin knowing verb, with a noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个名词是拉丁语「知道」动词的法语形式，再加名词词尾。

items.en: cognoscere meant to get to know.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为逐渐认识。

items.en: acointier meant to make someone known to another.
items.cn: acointier 意为使某人被另一人认识。

items.en: the noun acointance named the state of knowing someone.
items.cn: 名词 acointance 指认识某人的状态。

items.en: acquaintance entered English for both the person and the relation.
items.cn: acquaintance 在十四世纪进入英语，兼指那个人与那种关系。

items.en: the countable sense, a person, is now the most common.
items.cn: 如今最常用的是可数义，也就是「一个熟人」。

note.en: The first group is the acquaint family; the second is other words for people one knows.
note.cn: 第一组是 acquaint 词族；第二组是别的表示认识之人的词。

entries.definition: a person one works or deals with
a person who works with you

normalIntro.en: The word is the noun twin of acquaint, built on the Latin root for knowing.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 acquaint 的名词孪生兄弟，建在拉丁语「知道」词根上。

normal.en: acquaint is to make known, acquaintance is the one who is known.
normal.cn: acquaint 是使知道，acquaintance 是被认识的那个人。

normal.en: make the acquaintance of is the formal way to say meet.
normal.cn: make the acquaintance of 是「结识」的正式说法。

normal.en: a casual acquaintance is someone you greet but do not confide in.
normal.cn: casual acquaintance 是点头打招呼、却不会交心的人。

normal.en: acquaintance with facts is the uncountable, abstract use.
normal.cn: acquaintance with facts 是不可数的抽象用法。

normal.en: the plural acquaintances simply lists several such people.
normal.cn: 复数 acquaintances 只是列出好几个这样的人。

abstract.en: See a familiar face across the platform and a quick wave.
abstract.cn: 想象站台对面一张熟悉的脸，和你飞快地挥一下手。

abstract.en: Picture a name tag you can read but a story you cannot tell.
abstract.cn: 想象胸牌上的名字你看得清，他的故事你却讲不出。

abstract.en: Think of a thin thread linking two people who never quite became friends.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线连着两个人，他们始终没真正成为朋友。

examples.en: He is an acquaintance rather than a close friend.
examples.cn: 他是熟人，而不是密友。

examples.en: Her acquaintance with Chinese poetry surprised the class.
examples.cn: 她对中国古诗的了解让全班吃惊。

examples.en: They struck up an acquaintance during the long delay.
examples.cn: 在漫长的延误中，他们结识了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿昆腾斯」——阿昆在站台遇见熟人，热络地腾出一个座位。

root: 古法语 acointance，源自 acointier（使认识），再上溯拉丁语 cognoscere（知道）；本义是「相识的状态」，后指认识而不深交的人。

sensesIntro.en: One noun names the person, the knowledge and the thin relation between them.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词，分别指那个人、那份了解，以及两者之间那根细线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a known face with an unknown story.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张认得的脸，一段不知道的故事。

branches.en: the person you greet but do not confide in
branches.cn: 会打招呼却不会交心的人

branches.en: a working knowledge of maps or poetry
branches.cn: 对地图或古诗的实用了解

branches.en: the relation that starts at a summer school
branches.cn: 始于暑期学校的那种关系

branches.en: a person and the tie that holds him
branches.cn: 一个人以及牵着他的那根线

branches.en: knowing a subject and knowing a face
branches.cn: 懂一门学问与认得一张脸

intro.en: The French verb stem plus a noun ending gives the person and the state.
intro.cn: 法语动词词干加名词词尾，给出人与状态两种意思。

latinIntro.en: The knowing root cognoscere also yields recognize and cognition.
latinIntro.cn: 「知道」词根 cognoscere 也产生 recognize 与 cognition。

definition_en: to get something, often through effort, purchase or experience
core_image: 一只手把一件原本不属于自己的东西收进怀里
scene: 去年她买下了街角那家小书店。She acquired a small bookshop last year.
sceneCN: 这里的 acquire 是「收购」（第 3 个义项：买下企业或资产）；句意是去年她收购了一家小书店。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「收购；获得；习得」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「收购方」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「贪得的」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「后天获得的」

senses.title: To obtain an object or property
senses.definition: to come to own something that you did not have before
senses.definitionCN: 得到原本不属于自己的东西，成为它的主人
senses.example: He acquired a rare stamp at the auction.
senses.exampleCN: 他在拍卖会上得到一枚珍稀邮票。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to seek in addition, so the first sense is simply the end of a search: the thing is now yours.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「额外去寻求」，所以第一个义项就是寻求的终点：东西归你了。

senses.title: To learn a skill or body of knowledge
senses.definition: to come to have a skill or understanding through practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过练习逐渐拥有某种技能或理解
senses.example: Children acquire language without formal lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童不用正式上课就能习得语言。
senses.why: What is true of objects is true of abilities: they can be gained over time, so the verb moves from possessions to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 东西如此，能力也如此：它们可以随时间获得，于是这个动词从财物挪到了头脑。

senses.title: To buy up a company
senses.definition: to take control of a business by buying it
senses.definitionCN: 通过购买取得一家企业的控制权
senses.example: The group acquired three smaller rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 该集团收购了三家较小的竞争对手。
senses.why: In business the object grows large, but the grammar stays the same: one owner is replaced by another through a purchase.
senses.whyCN: 在商业里宾语变大了，语法却没变：通过一笔买卖，一个主人换成了另一个主人。

senses.title: To come to have a habit or name
senses.definition: to develop a habit, a taste or a reputation over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间形成习惯、口味或名声
senses.example: The town acquired a reputation for good bread.
senses.exampleCN: 这座镇子渐渐以好面包闻名。
senses.why: Reputation and habits are not bought, yet they are still gained; the verb treats them as things that settle on a person.
senses.whyCN: 名声与习惯不是买来的，却仍然是「得来」的；这个动词把它们当作落在人身上的东西。

intro.en: The word is Latin for seeking something in addition, built from a prefix and a verb of searching.
intro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语中意为「额外去寻求」，由一个前缀和一个表示寻找的动词构成。

items.en: quaerere meant to seek, to ask or to try to get.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻找、询问或设法取得。

items.en: acquirere added ad-, towards, to the same search.
items.cn: acquirere 在同一个「寻找」前加了表示朝向的 ad-。

items.en: the past participle acquisitus described what had been gained.
items.cn: 过去分词 acquisitus 形容已经取得的东西。

items.en: acquire entered English as a verb of obtaining.
items.cn: acquire 在十五世纪进入英语，是表示获得的动词。

items.en: it now covers property, skills, habits and corporate takeovers.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖财产、技能、习惯与企业收购。

note.en: The first group is the acquisition family; the second is other verbs of getting.
note.cn: 第一组是 acquisition 词族；第二组是别的表示获得的动词。

entries.definition: gained after birth or by effort

normalIntro.en: The Latin search verb quaerere is the root, also seen in inquire and require.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「寻找」动词 quaerere 是词根，inquire 与 require 里也能看到它。

normal.en: quaerere means to seek, so acquire is to end a search with a gain.
normal.cn: quaerere 意为寻找，所以 acquire 是带着收获结束寻找。

normal.en: acquisition is the noun, acquirer the buyer.
normal.cn: 名词是 acquisition，收购方是 acquirer。

normal.en: acquire knowledge and acquire skills are the learning pair.
normal.cn: acquire knowledge 与 acquire skills 是学习类的一对搭配。

normal.en: acquire a taste for means to grow to like something.
normal.cn: acquire a taste for 意为渐渐喜欢上某物。

normal.en: in business, acquire a company means to buy control of it.
normal.cn: 在商业里，acquire a company 意为买下它的控制权。

abstract.en: See a hand close around an object that was not there before.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手合拢，把原先不在手里的东西握住。

abstract.en: Picture a child picking up a new word each day.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子每天捡起一个新词。

abstract.en: Think of a shop sign being lowered and another raised above it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块招牌被摘下，另一块挂了上去。

examples.en: She acquired the painting for a modest sum.
examples.cn: 她花不多的钱得到了那幅画。

examples.en: Students acquire reading skills through daily practice.
examples.cn: 学生通过每日练习习得阅读技能。

examples.en: The chain acquired two local bakeries this spring.
examples.cn: 这家连锁店今年春天收购了两家本地面包房。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿快尔」——阿快眼疾手快，一把将看中的东西搂进怀里。

root: 拉丁语 acquirere（求得），由 ad-（朝向）与 quaerere（寻找、求取）构成；本义是「寻求而得到」，后引申为习得、养成与收购。

sensesIntro.en: One verb of getting covers things, skills, companies and reputations.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表示「得到」的动词，管着东西、技能、公司与名声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing on what it has sought.
core.cn: 核心意象：寻到手边，手合拢。

branches.en: a stamp or a painting now owned
branches.cn: 归到名下的邮票或画作

branches.en: a language or a skill learned by practice
branches.cn: 练出来的语言或技能

branches.en: a rival firm bought for control
branches.cn: 为取得控制权而买下的对手

branches.en: a habit or a name that settles on someone
branches.cn: 落在某人身上的习惯或名声

branches.en: small purchases and large takeovers share one verb
branches.cn: 小额购入与大型收购共用一个动词

intro.en: A Latin prefix and a verb of seeking build the word.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁前缀和一个表示寻找的动词，构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: quaerere, to seek, also underlies inquire, require and question.
latinIntro.cn: quaerere（寻找）也是 inquire、require 与 question 的底子。

definition_en: the act of gaining something, especially the buying of a company or the learning of a skill
core_image: 一份合同签完，另一家公司的招牌被换下来
scene: 收购那家对手公司，前后花了好几个月。The acquisition of the rival firm took months.
sceneCN: 这里的 acquisition 是「收购」（第 1 个义项：买下企业）；句意是收购对手公司花了几个月。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「获得；收购」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「收购方」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「贪得的」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「后天获得的」

senses.title: The buying of a company
senses.definition: the purchase of one business by another
senses.definitionCN: 一家企业买下另一家企业
senses.example: The acquisition added three factories to the group.
senses.exampleCN: 这次收购为集团增加了三家工厂。
senses.why: The noun turns the act of gaining into a business event, and in finance the most visible gain is a bought rival.
senses.whyCN: 名词把「取得」变成一个商业事件，而在金融里最显眼的取得，就是买下一家对手。

senses.title: The gaining of knowledge or skill
senses.definition: the process of coming to have information or an ability
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐拥有知识或能力的过程
senses.example: The acquisition of a new language takes years.
senses.exampleCN: 掌握一门新语言需要多年。
senses.why: What is bought in business is learned in the mind, so the same noun names the slow gaining of a skill.
senses.whyCN: 商业里用钱买的东西，在头脑里靠学得来，于是同一个名词也指技能缓慢到手的过程。

senses.title: Something newly obtained
senses.definition: an object that has recently been gained, especially by a museum
senses.definitionCN: 最近得到的东西，尤指博物馆的新藏品
senses.example: The painting is the museum's latest acquisition.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画是博物馆最新入藏的藏品。
senses.why: From the act comes the object: once the deal closes, the thing bought stands in the room and is called an acquisition.
senses.whyCN: 从行为落到物件：交易一完成，买来的东西就摆在屋里，被称作一件 acquisition。

intro.en: The noun is the Latin action noun of the verb for seeking and gaining.
intro.cn: 这个名词是拉丁语中「寻求并获得」动词的动作名词。

items.en: quaerere meant to seek.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻找。

items.en: acquirere meant to gain by seeking.
items.cn: acquirere 意为寻求而得到。

items.en: acquisitio named the act of gaining.
items.cn: acquisitio 指取得的行为。

items.en: acquisition entered English as a noun of obtaining.
items.cn: acquisition 在十五世纪进入英语，是表示获得的名词。

items.en: finance gave it the dominant sense of buying a company.
items.cn: 金融赋予了它「买下公司」这一主要含义。

note.en: The first group is the acquire family; the second is other words for a purchase or gain.
note.cn: 第一组是 acquire 词族；第二组是别的表示购买或获得的词。

entries.definition: the taking of control of a firm

normalIntro.en: The seeking root quaerere runs through the whole family.
normalIntro.cn: 表示寻找的词根 quaerere 贯穿整个词族。

normal.en: acquire is the verb, acquisition the event or the thing gained.
normal.cn: acquire 是动词，acquisition 是事件或得到的东西。

normal.en: merger and acquisition is the fixed phrase for corporate buying.
normal.cn: merger and acquisition 是企业并购的固定说法。

normal.en: language acquisition is the standard term in linguistics.
normal.cn: language acquisition 是语言学里的标准术语。

normal.en: a museum calls each new piece its latest acquisition.
normal.cn: 博物馆把每件新入藏的东西称作最新藏品。

normal.en: the plural acquisitions can mean several deals or several objects.
normal.cn: 复数 acquisitions 既可指多笔交易，也可指多件藏品。

abstract.en: See a sign being unscrewed and another lifted into place.
abstract.cn: 想象旧招牌被拧下来，新招牌被吊上去。

abstract.en: Picture a child adding one new word a day.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子每天增加一个新词。

abstract.en: Think of a glass case holding a newly bought painting.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃柜里放着一幅刚买来的画。

examples.en: The bank announced the acquisition of a smaller rival.
examples.cn: 银行宣布收购一家较小的竞争对手。

examples.en: Reading widely speeds the acquisition of vocabulary.
examples.cn: 广泛阅读能加快词汇的习得。

examples.en: The sculpture is the gallery's most valuable acquisition.
examples.cn: 这座雕像是画廊最珍贵的藏品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿快贼身」——阿快眼疾手快，把看中的东西一样样收进自己名下。

root: 拉丁语 acquisitio，源自 acquirere（求取），由 ad-（朝向）与 quaerere（寻找）构成；本义是寻求而获得，现代金融语境中常指收购。

sensesIntro.en: The noun names a deal, a learning process and the object that results.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词分别指一笔交易、一段学习过程，以及最后到手的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something sought coming into your hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：寻到的东西落进手里。

branches.en: one firm swallowing another
branches.cn: 一家公司吞下另一家

branches.en: years of picking up a language
branches.cn: 多年拾起一门语言

branches.en: the painting now in the glass case
branches.cn: 如今放在玻璃柜里的画

branches.en: the deal and the thing obtained by it
branches.cn: 交易与交易得来的东西

branches.en: learning and buying share one drive to gain
branches.cn: 学习与购买共享同一种求得的动力

intro.en: A Latin prefix, a seeking verb and a noun ending make the word.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁前缀、表示寻找的动词和一个名词词尾，构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: quaerere also gives inquire, require and question.
latinIntro.cn: quaerere 也给出 inquire、require 与 question。

definition_en: a unit of land area, or a piece of land measured in such units
core_image: 一头牛拉着犁，一天走完的那片方方正正的田
scene: 这个家庭农场占地约四十英亩。The family farm covers about forty acres.
sceneCN: 这里的 acre 是「英亩」（第 1 个义项：土地面积单位）；句意是这个家庭农场约有四十英亩。

derivatives.zh: 由 acre 加集合名词后缀构成，义为「英亩数；土地面积」
由 acre 加形容词词尾构成，义为「拥有田地的」（多见于旧文学）

senses.title: A unit of land area
senses.definition: a measure of land equal to about four thousand square metres
senses.definitionCN: 一种土地面积单位，约合四千平方米
senses.example: They keep two horses on five acres.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在五英亩地上养了两匹马。
senses.why: The Old English word named a field itself, and the measure grew out of how much land a team could plough in a day.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词本指一块田，而面积单位是从「一队牛一天能犁多少地」长出来的。

senses.title: Land or grounds
senses.definition: a stretch of land, often used in the plural for an estate
senses.definitionCN: 一片土地，常用复数指一整处地产
senses.example: The old house stands in acres of green lawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老房子坐落在成片绿草坪中。
senses.why: Because the word first meant a field, the plural can still mean land as property rather than a number on a survey.
senses.whyCN: 因为这词最初就指一块田，所以复数至今仍可指作为产业的土地，而不是图纸上的一个数字。

intro.en: The word is an old Germanic field term, related to Latin ager.
intro.cn: 这是一个古老的日耳曼语田地词，与拉丁语 ager 同源。

items.en: a reconstructed root meant field or pasture.
items.cn: 一个重构词根意为田地或牧场。

items.en: the root became a word for an open field.
items.cn: 这个词根变成表示开阔田地的词。

items.en: æcer meant a field, especially a ploughed one.
items.cn: æcer 意为田地，尤指犁过的田。

items.en: the word also became a fixed measure of land.
items.cn: 这个词同时也成了固定的土地面积单位。

items.en: acre now measures plots from gardens to farms.
items.cn: 如今 acre 丈量从园子到农场的各类地块。

note.en: The first group shares the acre stem; the second is other land measures and land words.
note.cn: 第一组共享 acre 词干；第二组是别的土地计量与土地词。

plots of land in the plural
the Latin word for a field

normalIntro.en: The word is cousin to Latin ager, field, and to agriculture.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词与拉丁语 ager（田地）以及 agriculture 是亲戚。

normal.en: æcer meant a ploughed field before it meant a measure.
normal.cn: æcer 先指犁过的田，后来才指面积单位。

normal.en: an acre is roughly the land a team could plough in a day.
normal.cn: 一英亩大致是一队牛一天能犁完的地。

normal.en: acreage is the collective noun for the size of a farm.
normal.cn: acreage 是表示农场面积的集合名词。

normal.en: per acre is the phrase used for crop yields.
normal.cn: per acre 是计算亩产的固定说法。

normal.en: the plural acres often suggests a large estate.
normal.cn: 复数 acres 常暗示一大片地产。

abstract.en: See an ox team turning at the end of a square field.
abstract.cn: 想象一队牛在方形田的尽头转弯。

abstract.en: Picture a farmhouse surrounded by a green sea of lawn.
abstract.cn: 想象农舍四周是一片绿色的草坪海。

abstract.en: Think of a deed with the land size written in acres.
abstract.cn: 想象一份地契，面积一栏写着英亩数。

examples.en: The vineyard covers thirty acres of hillside.
examples.cn: 这片葡萄园占了三十英亩山坡。

examples.en: They bought an acre of woodland behind the house.
examples.cn: 他们买下了屋后一英亩林地。

examples.en: The farmer counts every acre before planting.
examples.cn: 农民播种前把每一英亩都算清楚。

sensesIntro.en: A field word became a number, and the number still remembers the field.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「田」字变成了数字，而这个数字仍记得那片田。

branches.cn: 以大片英亩计的地产

branches.en: land at once counted and owned
branches.cn: 既被计数又被拥有的土地

intro.en: The word is a Germanic field term; its endings are English, not Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语的田地词，词尾是英语的，不是拉丁的。

latinIntro.en: Its distant Latin cousin is ager, field, which gives agriculture and agrarian.
latinIntro.cn: 它在拉丁语里的远亲是 ager（田地），后者给出 agriculture 与 agrarian。

definition_en: from one side of something to the other, or on the opposite side
core_image: 一条线从纸的左边一直划到右边
scene: 一座窄桥横跨在那条小河上。The bridge runs across the narrow river.
sceneCN: 这里的 across 是「横过」（第 1 个义项：从一边到另一边）；句意是这座桥横跨小河。

derivatives.zh: 由同源词根构成，义为「穿过；交叉」
由 cross 加名词后缀构成，义为「十字路口；横渡」

senses.title: From one side to the other
senses.definition: moving or reaching from one side of something to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从某物的一边移动到或延伸到另一边
senses.example: We walked across the square in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 我们冒雨走过广场。
senses.why: The word began as a phrase meaning in a cross, so the first sense is simply the line a crossbar makes from side to side.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是「成十字地」的短语，所以第一个义项就是横杆从一边划到另一边的那条线。

senses.title: On the opposite side
senses.definition: situated on the other side of a road, river or space
senses.definitionCN: 位于道路、河流或空间的另一边
senses.example: The bakery is across the road from my flat.
senses.exampleCN: 面包店就在我公寓的马路对面。
senses.why: Once you have crossed, you are standing on the far side, so the same word also marks position rather than movement.
senses.whyCN: 一旦穿过去，人就站在了那一边，于是同一个词也标记位置，而不只是动作。

senses.title: Throughout an area
senses.definition: in every part of a region or a group
senses.definitionCN: 在一个地区或群体的每个部分
senses.example: The news spread across the whole province.
senses.exampleCN: 消息传遍了全省。
senses.why: A line drawn across a map touches every point between the edges, and that picture grows into the sense of throughout.
senses.whyCN: 在地图上横着画一条线，会碰到两端之间的每一点，这幅图便长成「遍及」的意思。

senses.title: Over to this side, as an adverb
senses.definition: used alone to mean from the far side to here
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用，表示从对面到这边
senses.example: He swam across in less than a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他不到一分钟就游了过来。
senses.why: Without an object the word still keeps the full crossing in view, so it can stand alone as an adverb.
senses.whyCN: 不带宾语时，这个词心里仍装着整段横渡，所以能单独作副词用。

intro.en: The word began as an English phrase built on the French word for a cross.
intro.cn: 这个词最初是一个英语短语，建在法语表示「十字」的词上。

items.en: crux meant a cross or a gallows.
items.cn: crux 意为十字架或绞架。

items.en: croix meant a cross.
items.cn: 古法语 croix 意为十字。

items.en: the phrase a-crois meant in a cross or crosswise.
items.cn: 短语 a-crois 意为成十字地、横着。

items.en: across settled into one word for crossing from side to side.
items.cn: across 固定成一个词，表示从一边横到另一边。

items.en: it now also means opposite and throughout.
items.cn: 如今它也表示「在对面」与「遍及」。

note.en: The first group shares the cross root; the second is other words of passing or covering.
note.cn: 第一组共享 cross 词根；第二组是别的表示穿过或覆盖的词。

from one side to the other, often above

normalIntro.en: The word is a cross: a- plus the French croix.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一个十字：a- 加上法语 croix。

normal.en: croix is a cross, so across draws a line from side to side.
normal.cn: croix 是十字，所以 across 从一边划到另一边。

normal.en: across from is the fixed phrase for opposite.
normal.cn: across from 是表示「在对面」的固定短语。

normal.en: come across and run across both mean to meet by chance.
normal.cn: come across 与 run across 都表示偶然遇见。

normal.en: across the country means from coast to coast.
normal.cn: across the country 意为从东岸到西岸、全国范围。

normal.en: across the board means affecting every part equally.
normal.cn: across the board 意为全面地影响每一部分。

abstract.en: Draw one straight line from the left edge of a page to the right.
abstract.cn: 想象从纸的左缘到右缘划一条直线。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge lying flat over a narrow stream.
abstract.cn: 想象一座平躺在窄溪上的桥。

abstract.en: Think of a rumour moving from village to village.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传言从一村传到另一村。

examples.en: She ran across the field to meet us.
examples.cn: 她跑过田野来迎我们。

examples.en: The post office is across from the school.
examples.cn: 邮局在学校对面。

examples.en: The disease spread across the region in weeks.
examples.cn: 这种病几周内就传遍了整个地区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿跨斯」——阿跨一抬腿，就从马路这边跨到了那边。

root: 中古英语 a-crois，源自古法语 a croix（成十字地），更早出自拉丁语 crux（十字）；本义是横着划过去，引申为在对面、遍及。

sensesIntro.en: One crossbar line becomes a crossing, a position opposite, and a spread through a whole area.
sensesIntro.cn: 一条横杆线，先变成穿越，再变成对面的位置，最后变成铺满整片区域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn straight from side to side.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一边直直划到另一边的线。

branches.en: walking over a square in the rain
branches.cn: 冒雨走过广场

branches.en: the bakery standing on the far side
branches.cn: 站在马路对面的面包店

branches.en: news touching every village
branches.cn: 碰到每个村庄的消息

branches.en: a swimmer arriving without an object
branches.cn: 不带宾语时游过来的人

branches.en: movement and position on one line
branches.cn: 同一条线上的动作与位置

intro.en: An English prefix and a French cross make the word.
intro.cn: 一个英语前缀加一个法语的「十字」，构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: The French croix goes back to Latin crux, also the source of cross and crucial.
latinIntro.cn: 法语 croix 上溯拉丁语 crux，也是 cross 与 crucial 的来源。

definition_zh: 行动；表演；起作用；法案；一幕
definition_en: to do something, to perform a role, or a deed, law or part of a play
core_image: 舞台灯亮起，一个人从幕后迈出第一步
scene: 警报一响，她立刻行动起来。She acted quickly when the alarm sounded.
sceneCN: 这里的 act 是「采取行动」（第 1 个义项：做事、行动）；句意是警报响时她迅速行动。

derivatives.zh: 由词根加名词后缀构成，义为「行动」
由词根加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「男演员」
由 actor 加阴性后缀构成，义为「女演员」
由词根加形容词后缀构成，义为「活跃的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「活动」

senses.title: To take action
senses.definition: to do something rather than wait or talk
senses.definitionCN: 去做某事，而不是等待或空谈
senses.example: We must act before the chance is gone.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须在机会溜走前行动。
senses.why: The Latin verb agere means to drive or do, so the first sense is bare doing, the opposite of standing still.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 agere 意为驱动、做事，所以第一个义项就是单纯的「做」，与站着不动相对。

senses.title: To perform a role
senses.definition: to play a character on stage or in a film
senses.definitionCN: 在舞台或电影里扮演一个角色
senses.example: He acted the part of a tired king.
senses.exampleCN: 他扮演了一位疲惫的国王。
senses.why: Doing becomes pretending in the theatre: the actor drives a borrowed character through the story.
senses.whyCN: 「做」到了剧场里就变成「装作」：演员驱动一个借来的角色走完故事。

senses.title: To serve as or work on
senses.definition: to perform a function, often in the phrase act as
senses.definitionCN: 发挥某种作用，常用于 act as 这一说法
senses.example: The old barn acts as a workshop in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天那座旧谷仓充当工坊。
senses.why: A thing can do a job without being alive, so the verb extends from people to anything that fills a role.
senses.whyCN: 东西也能干活而不必有生命，于是这个动词从人扩展到一切填补某个角色的东西。

senses.title: A law passed by a parliament
senses.definition: a formal decision of a legislative body
senses.definitionCN: 立法机构作出的正式决定
senses.example: Parliament passed the act last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 议会去年春天通过了这项法案。
senses.why: A law is a deed done by a body of people, and the noun keeps that sense of something accomplished and binding.
senses.whyCN: 法律是一群人做成的一件事，名词因此保留了「已完成且具约束力」的意味。

senses.title: A division of a play
senses.definition: one of the main parts of a play or opera
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧或歌剧的主要段落之一
senses.example: The curtain falls at the end of the second act.
senses.exampleCN: 第二幕结束时幕布落下。
senses.why: The stage divides doing into chunks, and each chunk of action carries the name of action itself.
senses.whyCN: 舞台把「做」切成一段段，而每一段动作都直接沿用了「动作」这个名字。

intro.en: The word is Latin for a doing or a driven thing, from a verb meaning to drive.
intro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语中意为「做成之事」或「被驱动之物」，来自表示驱动的动词。

items.en: agere meant to drive, to lead or to do.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、带领或做事。

items.en: actus meant a doing, a deed or a movement.
items.cn: actus 意为行为、事迹或动作。

items.en: the same root gave agere's noun actionem, a doing.
items.cn: 同一词根也给出名词 actionem，意为行为。

items.en: act entered English for a deed and for a division of a play.
items.cn: act 进入英语，兼指行为与戏剧的一幕。

items.en: the legal sense, a statute, developed in the language of parliament.
items.cn: 法律义「法令」在议会语言中发展出来。

items.en: the verb now covers doing, pretending and serving as.
items.cn: 如今这个动词涵盖做事、演戏与充当。

note.en: The first group is the action family; the second is other words for deeds and performing.
note.cn: 第一组是 action 词族；第二组是别的表示行为与表演的词。

normalIntro.en: The Latin agere, to drive, is the root of the whole action family.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere（驱动）是整个 action 词族的根。

normal.en: agere means to drive, so act is to set something moving.
normal.cn: agere 意为驱动，所以 act 就是让事情动起来。

normal.en: actor, action and active all carry the same act stem.
normal.cn: actor、action、active 都带同一个 act 词干。

normal.en: act as introduces the role, act on introduces the reason.
normal.cn: act as 引出角色，act on 引出依据。

normal.en: an act of parliament is a law, not a performance.
normal.cn: an act of parliament 是法律，不是演出。

normal.en: a play is divided into acts, just as work is divided into deeds.
normal.cn: 戏分成幕，正如工作分成一件件事。

abstract.en: See a figure step out of the wings into the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人从侧幕走进灯光里。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching for the alarm switch.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向警报开关。

abstract.en: Think of a law book open at one stamped page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本法律书摊开在盖了章的一页。

examples.en: The city acted at once to repair the bridge.
examples.cn: 市政当局立刻行动，修复了这座桥。

examples.en: She acts in a small theatre on weekends.
examples.cn: 她周末在一家小剧场演戏。

examples.en: The new act limits the use of the river.
examples.cn: 这项新法案限制了这条河的用途。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克特」——阿克特爱演戏，灯一亮就从幕后大步迈出来。

root: 拉丁语 actus（行为、动作），源自 agere（驱动、做）；本义是「做成之事」，后分化为行动、表演、起作用、法案与戏剧的一幕。

sensesIntro.en: One root of doing covers a deed, a role, a function, a law and a chunk of theatre.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「做」的词根，管着一件事、一个角色、一种作用、一条法律和一段戏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step taken out of the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：从暗处迈出的一步。

branches.en: a decision turned into movement
branches.cn: 变成动作的决定

branches.en: a borrowed character on stage
branches.cn: 舞台上借来的角色

branches.en: an old barn doing the work of a workshop
branches.cn: 充当工坊的旧谷仓

branches.en: a law stamped by parliament
branches.cn: 议会盖章的法律

branches.en: one block of story before the curtain
branches.cn: 落幕前的一段故事

intro.cn: 一个表示驱动的拉丁词根，加上名词与形容词词尾，撑起整个词族。

latinIntro.cn: agere（驱动）也给出 agent、agenda 与 agile。
